data.narrative:
Wayve is a Series D autonomous systems company founded by Amar Shah and Alex Kendall. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 4 same-sector peers at similar valuation tiers within Drones & Autonomous, spanning both private (Zipline at $7.6B Series H, Nuro at $6.0B Series G) and public entities (Joby Aviation at $6.9B, Archer Aviation at $3.3B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. The Stage-Progression method, anchored to Wayve's last post-money of $8.6B, applies a typical Series D-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.5x, implying $12.9B. The Peer-Median method yields $6.4B, the median across the 4-company comp set, with a range from $3.3B to $7.6B reflecting variation in stage maturity and market positioning within the sector.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $5.5B (low) to $14.8B (high), with a median of $9.7B. The $8.6B current valuation sits within this range but toward the lower-to-mid point, reflecting tension between stage-typical step-up progression and peer positioning. Key uncertainties include heterogeneity in deployment maturity across the comp set and timing of next-stage funding events, which influence both peer valuations and applicable stage multiples.
